dek: Eight Yellowstone waterfalls, from the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone to Mystic and Wraith Falls. See walk lengths, fees and when snowmelt peaks.
overview: Yellowstone became the first national park on March 1, 1872. Most of the park sits at 6,000 feet or higher, and the park's weather page says snow is possible in every month, so conditions can change quickly.

We cover eight waterfalls here, all in Wyoming: the canyon falls (the Upper and Lower Falls of the Yellowstone River), Undine Falls, Wraith Falls, Mystic Falls, Firehole Falls, Moose Falls, and Albright Falls in the Bechler area. USGS names Albright Falls for the park's first civilian superintendent, and it has no trail details or reviews in our files.
fallsIntro: Mystic Falls and Wraith Falls are the two with published walk lengths. The canyon falls draw the biggest crowds but don't have a trail length in our files.
plan: For an easy stroll, Wraith Falls is 0.4 mile one way. For a half day, Mystic Falls is 2.4 miles round trip. The park rates it moderately strenuous, with a modest climb to the falls and about 500 feet more if you continue up to the overlook.

The Upper Falls of the Yellowstone River is the one with a season on file: late spring and early summer for peak snowmelt. Park roads are seasonal, so check which ones are open before you plan around it.
flow: The Gibbon River gauge at Madison Junction (06037100) is under a mile from Firehole Falls. Between 2019 and 2024 its average daily flow peaked in May at about 247 cubic feet per second and was lowest in February at about 87. That fits the late spring snowmelt season.
It is one river in one part of the park, so it says more about Firehole Falls than about the canyon falls or the Bechler area.
feesLead: An entrance pass is required, but vehicle reservations are not. Visitors who are not US residents pay an added per-person fee on the park's 2026 fee page.
access: You can buy a pass before you arrive or at an entrance station. Because the park sits so high, the weather page says spring and fall daytime temperatures often run from the teens to the 60s Fahrenheit, and a foot of snow in a day is not unusual.
safety: Mystic Falls is the hike with a posted rating: the park calls it moderately strenuous. The Upper Falls adds seasonal roads. This guide doesn't cover the park's rules for thermal areas, so read those on the park's website before you go.
